name: Singapore Management University
description: Singapore Management University is a publicly funded university established in 2000, with a city campus in Singapore's Bras Basah district. It specialises in business, economics, accountancy, law, computing and the social sciences, taught in a seminar-style format.
whyIncluded: One of Singapore's Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded Autonomous Universities, and the local reference point for business, economics and law degrees that Singaporean students often compare with overseas alternatives.

programmes.name: Master of Science in Financial Economics (MSFE)
programmes.notes: Self-funded programme: one tuition fee for all nationalities, no MOE-subsidised Citizen/PR rate. Official School of Economics MSFE page, 'Programme Fees' table: 'Tuition Fee for January 2027 Intake' S$54,500 inclusive of GST for the whole programme (billed S$21,800 + S$16,350 + S$16,350), with no separate SC/PR column, so the same tuition is recorded under citizen, pr and international; divided here by the 18-month full-time duration (flexible to 12 months). feeYear 2026 covers the January 2027 (AY2026/27) intake. The only Citizen/PR difference the page publishes is the one-off non-refundable registration fee on acceptance: S$400 incl. GST for Singapore Citizens/PRs, S$500 for international students (the page labels the S$500 'exclusive of GST'; the stated amount is recorded); the S$5,000 deposit contributes to tuition and is not counted separately. MOE check (2026-10-01): MOE's Tuition Grant Scheme page (moe.gov.sg/financial-matters/tuition-grant-scheme, updated 23 Jun 2026) covers 'selected full-time diploma and undergraduate courses' only; MOE parliamentary replies of 10 Jan 2023 and 24 Sep 2025 state that only around 20% of master's-by-coursework programmes at the autonomous universities are MOE-subsidised (profession-entry or sector-agency-aligned programmes) and the rest are non-subsidised; SMU's own list of MOE-subsidised graduate programmes (graduatestudies.smu.edu.sg/research-masters/programme-fees) contains only MPhil programmes, not the MSFE. The MSFE page's 'Discounts' section lists only a 10% SMU/SUTD alumni discount and says SMU may amend discount schemes per cohort. SMU's central 25th-anniversary scheme (media release 29 Oct 2024, 'from January 2025 onwards') advertises a S$5,000 discount for Singapore Citizens/PRs on the base fee before GST, not combinable with other discounts, but the MSFE programme page does not list it, its alumni discount differs from the central scheme, and SMU's discount calculator says discounts 'may vary depending on the specific programme', so no SC/PR net fee is derived here; a citizen or PR should ask SMU whether that discount applies to the MSFE. The page states the August 2027 intake fee rises to S$57,700 incl. GST (also shown on masters.smu.edu.sg/msfe as 'from August 2027 intake onwards') and that from AY2027 an annual miscellaneous fee of S$400 (SC/PR) or S$480 (international), excl. GST, replaces the registration fee. SMU's sites block bots, so the official pages were read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01, hence sourceType secondary. No earlier intake's fee is published, and no usable archived copy exists: the Wayback Machine index (checked 2026-10-01) holds only bot-blocked or redirect captures of economics.smu.edu.sg/msfe and none of masters.smu.edu.sg/msfe, so no 2024 or 2025 feeHistory rows could be recorded.

programmes.name: Master of Science in Applied Finance (MAF)
programmes.notes: No MOE subsidy (self-funded programme), but the official Lee Kong Chian School of Business MAF page publishes one tuition fee plus a nationality discount, so the Citizen/PR tiers are recorded net of that discount. Tuition fee S$63,220 inclusive of GST for the whole programme (Programme Fees table); the 'Discounts' section states 'Singaporean citizens and Permanent Residents are eligible for a one-time discount of S$5,000', applicable to students joining from the January 2025 intake onwards, one discount per student (the higher applies if several qualify, e.g. the S$8,000 SMU alumni discount), and 'deductable before Goods and Services Tax (GST)'. Derivation: S$63,220 / 1.09 = S$58,000 before GST, less S$5,000 = S$53,000, plus 9% GST = S$57,770 incl. GST for Citizens/PRs; international students pay the full S$63,220 (an ASEAN citizen discount of S$3,000 exists but is not applied here). Both divided by the 18-month full-time duration (24 months part-time): S$38,513.33 (citizen/pr) and S$42,146.67 (international) per year. The only intake shown is August 2027 (applications September 2026 to May 2027), hence feeYear 2027; the page says the August 2027 fees are indicative and subject to revision. Compulsory fees = annual Miscellaneous Fees for AY2027: S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$480 (international), excl. GST. The S$8,000 advance tuition fee contributes to the first tuition billing and is not counted separately; application fee S$100 excluded. SMU's sites block bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01, hence sourceType secondary. Fee history: the 2024 rows (August 2024 intake, AY2024/25) come from a Wayback Machine copy of SMU's official MAF programme page (web.archive.org capture 20240722135036 of masters.smu.edu.sg/programme/msc-in-applied-finance, read on 2026-10-01): tuition fee S$54,500 inclusive of GST for the whole programme (S$36,333.33 per year over 18 months), the same for all nationalities (the only discount then was S$5,000 for SMU alumni, so no Citizen/PR deduction is made for 2024), plus a one-off registration fee of S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$500 (international) incl. GST and no annual miscellaneous fee; the S$5,000 advance tuition fee counted towards tuition. No archived copy of the page for the August 2025 intake exists (business.smu.edu.sg captures are bot-block pages), so no 2025 rows.

programmes.name: Master of IT in Business (MITB)
programmes.notes: No MOE subsidy (self-funded programme), but the official SMU MITB page publishes one tuition fee plus a nationality discount, so the Citizen/PR tiers are recorded net of that discount. 'Programme Fees' section: total tuition S$56,680 inclusive of 9% GST for the whole programme, one figure for all nationalities; the 'Discounts' section lists a 'Nationality Discount' of S$5,000 for 'Singapore Citizen / Permanent Residents' (S$3,000 for ASEAN), applicable from the January 2025 intake onwards, one discount per student (the higher applies if several qualify, e.g. S$8,000 for SMU alumni), applied evenly across the three tuition billings and 'deductable before Goods and Services Tax (GST)'. Derivation: S$5,000 before GST = S$5,450 incl. 9% GST, so Citizens/PRs pay S$56,680 - S$5,450 = S$51,230 incl. GST; international students pay S$56,680. Full-time duration is 12 months (payment schedule 'Full-time (1 year)'; a 16-month full-time and a 24-month part-time option exist), so the whole-programme fee equals the annual figure. The payment schedule shows the same S$56,680 for both the January 2027 and August 2027 intakes; feeYear 2026 covers the January 2027 (AY2026/27) intake, and the page says the August 2027 figures are indicative. One-off fee = non-refundable registration fee: S$400 (Singapore Citizens/PRs) or S$500 (foreigners); from the August 2027 intake it is replaced by an annual miscellaneous fee of S$400 (SC/PR) or S$480 (foreigners), excl. GST. The S$10,000 deposit (S$8,000 from August 2027) forms part of the tuition fee and is not counted separately; application fee S$100 and textbooks excluded. SMU's sites block bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01 (the proxy returned only the page header, which confirms the S$56,680 fee; the discount wording was confirmed on the Wayback Machine copy of the same page, capture 20251204094943), hence sourceType secondary. Fee history, from Wayback Machine copies of this same official page read on 2026-10-01: 2024 rows = capture 20240301122616 and 20241114211818, total tuition S$52,320 incl. 9% GST, the same for all nationalities (the Citizen/PR discount only started with the January 2025 intake, so none is deducted for the August 2024 intake; a January 2025 entrant paid S$52,320 less the S$5,450 discount incl. GST), registration fee S$400/S$500; 2025 rows = capture 20250603095849, total tuition S$54,500 incl. 9% GST 'payable from the August 2025 intake onwards', Citizen/PR net S$54,500 - S$5,450 = S$49,050, registration fee S$400/S$500.

programmes.name: Juris Doctor (JD)
programmes.notes: Self-funded graduate-entry law degree (no MOE Tuition Grant). Official Yong Pung How School of Law page 'Finance & Administrative Matters for JD Programme, Admit Year 2026': tuition fee for the entire programme S$81,750 incl. GST, the same for all nationalities, billed in four instalments over the first two years (S$5,000 advance deposit + S$15,437.50 + 3 x S$20,437.50); divided here by the 3-year full-time candidature. One-off fee = non-refundable registration fee on offer acceptance: S$400 for Singaporeans/PRs, S$500 for international students. Textbooks and course materials are extra. The page lists discounts only for SMU alumni (S$8,000 from the 2025 intake), alumni course exemptions and SUTD alumni (10%), with no Singapore Citizen/PR discount, and states there is no government subsidy (e.g. MOE Tuition Grant) for the programme. law.smu.edu.sg blocks bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01 (figures re-verified unchanged, also on the school's 'Fees' page law.smu.edu.sg/jd/admissions/fees: '$81,750' for the 2026 intake), hence sourceType secondary. Only the 2026 admit year is published live. Fee history: the 2025 rows come from the Wayback Machine copy of this same official page titled 'Finance & Administrative Matters for JD Programme Admit Year 2025' (web.archive.org capture 20250702042339, read on 2026-10-01): tuition fee for the entire programme S$76,300 inclusive of GST, the same for all nationalities (S$5,000 deposit + S$14,075 + 3 x S$19,075), divided by the 3-year candidature = S$25,433.33 per year; registration fee S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$500 (international). No archived copy for the 2024 admit year exists, so no 2024 rows.

programmes.name: Master of Laws (LLM)
programmes.notes: No MOE subsidy (self-funded programme), but the official SMU LLM 'Fees & Scholarships' page publishes one tuition fee plus a Citizen/PR discount, so the Citizen/PR tiers are recorded net of that discount. Tuition fee for the August 2027 intake S$39,240 incl. GST for the whole one-year programme (Judicial Studies, Cross-Border Business and Finance Law in Asia, and Law and Technology tracks), the same for all nationalities; the page says the 2027 figure is indicative and subject to revision. Under 'Financial Assistance' it lists a 'Singapore Citizens/ Permanent Residents Discount: S$5,000 discount off total tuition fees (from 2025 intake onwards)' (also S$8,000 for SMU alumni/staff and S$3,000 for ASEAN nationals; discounts are not stackable with each other or with scholarships, and only the higher one applies). Derivation: S$39,240 - S$5,000 = S$34,240 for Citizens/PRs, taken literally off the GST-inclusive total because the page states no before-GST treatment (if SMU deducts it before GST the net would be S$33,790); international students pay S$39,240. The fee includes a non-refundable S$8,000 tuition deposit, which is not counted separately. Compulsory fees = annual miscellaneous fees from the 2027 intake: S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$480 (foreigners), excl. GST. Application fee S$100 excluded. The Dual LLM (Singapore & London) track costs S$37,605 to SMU plus GBP 22,975 to QMUL. law.smu.edu.sg blocks bots, so the official page was read through a reader proxy (r.jina.ai) on 2026-10-01 (figures re-verified unchanged), hence sourceType secondary. Fee history: the 2025 rows come from the Wayback Machine copy of this same official page (web.archive.org capture 20250602161614, read on 2026-10-01): 'For 2025 Intake S$38,150 Inclusive of GST (9%)' (S$5,000 deposit + S$14,075 in August + S$19,075 in December), the same Citizen/PR discount of S$5,000 'from 2025 intake onwards' giving S$33,150, and a one-off registration fee of S$400 (Singaporeans/PRs) or S$500 (foreigners) incl. GST instead of an annual miscellaneous fee. No archived copy for the 2024 intake exists, so no 2024 rows.
